trigger: operator hits the upgrade window this change documents and follows the new §4 sentence 'confirm before restarting during an upgrade, or resolve the pair via revoke afterward'
summary: HARMFUL OPERATOR GUIDANCE. The only revoke engine-principals.md defines is §6 'Revoke (terminal)' -- DELETE /api/v1/engine-principals/{id} -- which revokes EVERY active credential and then flips the identity to revoked, irreversibly (:173-185). The engine-principal route family has NO per-credential revoke (rest-api.md:919 enumerates credentials / credentials-rotate / credentials-confirm / transfer-owner; no DELETE). The one surface that can revoke a single engine credential, DELETE /api/v1/tokens/{id}, is not mentioned in this document at all. So an operator in exactly the state the paragraph addresses, following the paragraph, destroys the principal and both credentials. The CORRECT action is to do nothing: if the successor was picked up the sweep auto-revokes the predecessor and the cutover completes; if it was not, the UP-5 guard leaves both active and warns. Neither ends at zero credentials -- what is lost is the attestation, not access. SECOND OCCURRENCE OF THIS CLASS ON THIS BRANCH: the prior fix round's commit is titled 'correct guidance that recommended the one unsafe use' and it corrected authentication.md while leaving this file. Fixing named sites instead of sweeping for the claim.

trigger: both this branch and the sibling feat/auth-rotation-clock-guard declare api_token_store migration {3, ...} (origin/dev is at v2); the second to merge is not renumbered
summary: PgMigrationRunner::run is `if (m.version <= current) continue;` against a SCALAR high-water mark in public.schema_meta -- no applied-set table, no duplicate check, no monotonicity assertion (pg_migration_runner.cpp:194-262). The second {3,...} is skipped SILENTLY: any_applied is already true so not even the debug 'up to date' line prints, run() returns true, open_ = true, and the server BOOTS CLEAN. If this branch loses, kTokenColsTail unconditionally names rotation_initiator, so all ten SELECTs against api_tokens fail with 'column does not exist' (reproduced live on postgres:18) -- including get_by_hash, so validate_token returns nullopt, indistinguishable from 'no such token'. TOTAL API-token and engine-credential authentication outage on a server that reported a clean boot. Asymmetry that makes it worse: server.cpp:2751 refuses to start when a migration FAILS, but nothing detects one silently SKIPPED. THE RUNNER'S BRIEF WAS WRONG ON A MATERIAL POINT: I told consistency-auditor this branch carries an in-code note about the collision. It does not -- it grepped and found none; the note exists ONLY on the sibling. A merge-order rule recorded on one of two colliding sides does not reach the reviewer of the other, and the reviewer who needs it is precisely this one. Durable fix all three reporters converge on: make the runner fail closed on a duplicate or non-monotonic version (issue #3013). Second, independently proposed by two: a projection smoke-read in the constructor (SELECT kTokenColsTail ... LIMIT 0) failing open_ closed, which generalises to every future skipped or partial migration.

trigger: any open transaction holding ACCESS SHARE on api_tokens when the new binary boots -- i.e. the outgoing replica during a rolling upgrade, which reads api_tokens on every authenticated request
summary: ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, so the boot migration can be lock-timed-out by the outgoing replica. MEASURED live against postgres:18 with a reader holding an open transaction: 'ERROR: canceling statement due to lock timeout' at the pool's lock_timeout = 10000 (pg_pool.hpp:94). Propagates correctly: exec_ok fails, runner returns false, open_ = false, server.cpp:2751 refuses to start with a clear message. LOUD AND SELF-LIMITING -- a container restart is the natural retry, and the ALTER itself is instantaneous on a populated table (PG fast-default; new rows correctly read back ''), so only lock ACQUISITION is at risk, not a rewrite. Non-blocking, but this is the first DDL on the hottest table in a while and warrants a line of upgrade guidance.

trigger: no test runs the v2->v3 ALTER against a database genuinely at v2 with rows in it
summary: All five new tests clone apitoken_pg_template, which is ALREADY at v3; the pre-v3 case is modelled by UPDATE ... SET rotation_initiator = '' on a v3 schema. Nothing exercises the actual upgrade -- the only state a real deployment produces, and where both the migration collision and the lock-timeout live. YUZU_REQUIRE_PG_DB (fresh, non-template) is the documented vehicle for migration-behaviour tests and this file already has one ('ApiTokenStore reports !is_open on a migration failure'). Also the natural place to pin the proposed schema assertion. The five tests are otherwise strong: the disagreement case, wrong-operator-after-restart, and the F4-stays-RAM-only assertion are the right things to pin.

The error string's FIRST remedy is unreachable in every state that can now produce it. 'rotation confirmation unavailable — retry via rotate or fall back to revoke': every reaching state is a live kPair/kPairInGroup with two active rows, so 'retry via rotate' lands on the 2-active arm and errors. Only revoke works. This PR's own new docs say so correctly, so shipped prose and shipped error string now disagree about the remedy. String is pre-existing and untouched, but #2961 narrows its causes to exactly the set where the first remedy cannot help. Changing it means adding a key to engine_store_error_class.hpp and re-running the substring-collision check.

The rationale names a consequence that cannot occur: 'try_reserve's raw-secret re-serve MUST NEVER call this ... or a restart would resurrect a one-time-reveal contract'. resolve_rotation_initiator returns an identity string only and the raw secret is never persisted, so a try_reserve that consulted it still could not re-serve anything -- it fails on the grace-cache lookup first, as this PR's own test states. The boundary rule is sound; the stated consequence overstates it.

Under the ledger schema an external-model row must carry a reporter_ref the author does not control, precisely because otherwise it is a claim about independent review made by the reviewed. Recorded because this run exists to make the record auditable and that adjudication is what currently releases a residual. The reviewer separately judged the residual itself CORRECTLY adjudicated on the merits: the pre-#2961 coupling was accidental (the RAM entry is populated after commit but before the response is written, so even pre-fix a lost-response caller who recovered the id could confirm on the same process), and the rejected last_used_at != 0 guard genuinely cannot separate 'received but not deployed' from 'never received'.

adjudication_rationale: Negative results, recorded deliberately: three reviewers attacked the core mechanism independently and none could widen it. These are the properties a Gate 8 re-review must not regress.
summary: NO DEFECT on the mechanism itself. (1) ONE resolver, not two: resolve_rotation_initiator (:834) is the sole path and both confirm_rotation (:1323, engine) and confirm_token_rotation (:1957, human) call it and nothing else -- not the dispatch_confined_arms two-copies-drift shape. (2) Does not widen who can confirm: the only writers are the two mint INSERTs with value requesting_user, and all four production call sites pass session->username, never a body/query/proto field. The empty guard sits AFTER branch selection so RAM-empty, durable-empty and both-empty all fail closed; no caller treats nullopt as permission. Under RBAC off (the default) the change strictly STRENGTHENS the control -- pre-fix a post-restart confirm was refused for everyone, post-fix for everyone except the original initiator. (3) Read-failure vs absence holds STRUCTURALLY: a failed read never reaches the resolver, because read_active_for_principal_on_conn's empty-on-error is consumed one level up and maps to the retryable 'no in-flight rotation to confirm'. Upgrade window resolves to LOCKOUT, not bypass -- there is no input that makes '' match. (4) No partial-application window: the stamp is a column of the successor's own INSERT in the same transaction as the predecessor's pair-stamp, and all four clears sit inside pg_advisory_xact_lock transactions committing atomically with their revoke. (5) Schema vs readers: one projection (kTokenColsTail) and one materialiser (read_token), ten sites each, positionally aligned; no second path builds an ApiToken from SQL. (6) Error taxonomy: the diff is COMMENT-ONLY in engine_store_error_class.hpp, mcp_server.cpp and rotation_confirm_state.hpp; no substring added, ordering hazard respected, no terminal->Transient or transient->Conflict regression.

trigger: ApiTokenStore destructs with a live in-grace-window secret resident
summary: ApiTokenStore has NO destructor, so the grace cache holding RotationGraceEntry::raw (a one-time secret in a plain std::string) is freed without yuzu::secure_zero at teardown. All three EXPLICIT release paths are correct -- evict_rotation_raw, store_rotation_raw's overwrite, and scrub_elapsed_grace_secrets all scrub before freeing. Teardown is the one uncovered exit, and this diff's new tests are the FIRST in the suite to destruct a store with a live secret resident. SecureBuffer exists in-tree for exactly this. Pre-existing; pairs with the documented gap that only rotate_token has the ScopeExit scrub_secrets guard while rotate_engine_credential has none. Track both together as the in-code comment already suggests. Explicitly NOT the new-manual-cleanup policy floor: the diff adds no manual cleanup.

summary: RUN-LEVEL DEFECT, not a change defect. cpp-safety reviewed feat/auth-rotation-confirm-durability while a fix-round junior was mutating the same working tree, and reported an in-flight edit as pre-existing on origin/dev -- a claim that, if believed, would have de-gated the run's top blocking finding on BOTH branches. Also affected happy-path on #2964, which was told it could build in a worktree an active fix agent owned; it happened to catch a clean tree. Rule going forward: a review agent and a mutating agent never share a worktree -- give the reviewer a detached checkout at a named sha, or hold the tree.
